groups.description: Real SharedTree schema and mutation behavior

checks.requirement: Preserve protected UI, build, dependency, and grading assets.
Use the selected pinned SharedTree SDK without modifying it.
Pass native compilation or type checking and app build.
Store nested incident and step objects in real SharedTree arrays.
Represent a removed assignee as an absent optional field.
Edit individual properties without replacing unrelated subtrees or serializing the board.
Create an incident with a unique immutable ID, open status, and no steps or assignee.
Edit an incident title as a whole string.
Change status among open, investigating, and resolved.
Set an assignee, including an empty string distinct from absence.
Remove an existing optional assignee.
Delete an incident; repeated deletion does nothing.
Append a step with a unique immutable ID and completion false.
Edit a checklist step label as a whole string.
Set and clear a checklist step completion flag.
Delete a step; repeated deletion does nothing.
Move incidents before a sibling or to the end in either direction.
Move steps within an incident before a sibling or to the end in either direction.
Moving an item before itself does nothing.
Report invalid input visibly without changing the document.
Preserve native node identities and immutable IDs across moves.
After a sibling moves or disappears, edit the intended node rather than its old array index.
Edits targeting removed items do not affect another item or resurrect the removed node.
Show real remote edits from either client without reload.
Observe sequential shared moves and retain correct item targeting.
Verify both clients submitted real operations before releasing held remote delivery.
Concurrent edits to distinct existing properties both survive.
Concurrent inserts survive with distinct identities.
Concurrent same-property edits converge to a submitted value without prescribing a winner.
A late client sees the existing document.
After another client receives edits and both originals close, a fresh browser context reopens the expected service-backed content.
Opening an existing document does not initialize or reset it.
Close unsubscribes, closes the native session, and leaves controls inert.
Callbacks arriving after Close do not reactivate the session.
Creation, opening, and service errors remain visible without automatic creation retries.
